_comment: Harness config. limits: the Big-plan spend caps (USD) the proxy enforces per workflow run and per rolling week. models: what CodeAF may use, served to it by `harness proxy` as an OpenRouter-shaped catalog; prices are USD per million tokens, from https://synthetic.new/pricing, checked 2026-11-05. api_input/api_cached/api_output are the API list (overage) rates: every cost figure and cap in the factory uses them (the owner's decision, 2026-10-20). input/output/cache_read are the synthetic.new SUBSCRIPTION rates, kept for reference only. 'id' is what CodeAF sees; 'upstream' is the synthetic.new model id. 'max_concurrent': how many calls the factory sends each model at once, the proxy queuing calls past it. synthetic.new no longer has a fixed per-model cap (October 2026 pricing change: concurrency is by plan priority, Big highest, with throttling to protect the service), so 8 is our own first step up from the old cap of 2, raised further only while upstream 429s stay rare; CodeAF retries a 429. queue.max_parallel_runs is how many CodeAF runs the queue may have going at once; each run gets its own slice of every model's max_concurrent (perRunSlots: max(1, max_concurrent/max_parallel_runs), what task.parallel is set to) and its own worker seat, chosen by the lane the queue assigns. searches_per_run caps the web searches one run may run and search_max_uses_per_call the searches within one call; search goes through hosted Otari (the proxy declares otari_web_search inside the model call, issue #2), not through a separate endpoint, and each search costs limits.search_price_usd, so searches draw credit; the caps wall off a runaway loop (issue #58). planner (issue #61): when the queue sees fewer than min_backlog codeaf-queued issues open and no plan run started within min_hours, harness plan-check tells the queue job to dispatch one CodeAF run in plan mode (a read-only pass whose proposals are labelled codeaf-proposed, never codeaf-queued); max_proposals caps what one plan run may propose. alerts (issue #131): the thresholds the model-stats routine alerts on. They are config and not code because a threshold is a judgement about the service, not a fact about the code: synthetic.new can degrade, a plan can change, and the owner must be able to move a threshold in a reviewed config file without a code change. Every field is optional and means the issue #131 value when the block is absent, so a models.json written before the block still loads; main.go's validator refuses an absurd value naming the field. hour_calls is how many calls an hour needs before its first-token p50 is judged at all; ttft_p50_ratio compares an hour's p50 against the model's own trailing baseline (ttft_p50_ratio_baseline_hours) and ttft_p90_ms alerts on a p90 above 15 s. The decode figures count only completions of decode_min_tokens or more, so a short call measures its own overhead rather than throughput, and decode_ratio alerts when decode p50 drops below that fraction of the baseline over decode_baseline_hours. stall_gap_ms is the silence between streamed lines that counts as a stall, and stall_pct the share of turns carrying one that alerts. rate_429_pct is the rate above which the factory should lower max_concurrent rather than raise it; reject_pct is the share of hostile or unusable rows refused before the report is built. slot_waits_per_run alerts on a run that queued for a model slot more often than that, and any abandoned wait alerts whatever it says. window_hours is the default window the routine reports over.

alerts._comment: Thresholds the model-stats routine alerts on (issue #131). Each field is optional: an absent block, or a field this file does not carry, uses the issue #131 value the validator in main.go fills in, so a models.json written before this block still loads and still alerts. A count-shaped field written as 0 is refused, not defaulted (a written 0 would silently disable its alert); a percentage or ratio written as 0 means its default, the same as leaving it out. Percentages are percent, not fractions: 1.0 is one percent.

limits.plan_note: Big plan $90/mo. Chat goes through hosted Otari (https://eu.api.otari.ai/api/v1), which fronts the same synthetic.new models and enforces the organisation's own budget and balance, so the proxy no longer polls synthetic.new's /v2/quotas and the old min_credit_percent floor is gone. All figures and caps here are at the API list (overage) prices, the owner's decision on 2026-10-20: CostOf prices calls at api_*; the input/output/cache_read subscription rates are reference only. weekly_credit_usd 100 is maxCredits x 4.5, the measured overage/subscription ratio for the factory's model mix (2026-10-17..19; DeepSeek alone is ~7.9x), and run_credit_usd 5 is about 2.5x the most expensive run seen at overage prices ($1.97); both are the factory's own cheap runaway guards: when a cap is reached the proxy refuses further calls (it does not only pace the queue). overage_usd 0 = stop rather than pay past the weekly credit.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: low, minimal and medium are sent as medium (owner's decision, 2026-10-17): measured on a real multi-step Go edit-and-test task (issue #24, 3 repeats per case) medium saved 19.3% median completion tokens and 17.8% median wall time at equal correctness, and about 72% of this model's output is reasoning. low is never sent raw: GLM returns empty answers at low

models.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 10/17 checkpoint (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role mid, the default DeepSeek model since 2026-10-31 (owner's decision, after the 1017 vs v4.1-flash experiment: all 16 runs passed, at about a third of the calls and cost per run; first-token latency about 6x slower). Added 2026-10-20 from synthetic.new's /openai/v1/models: same API prices, context and efforts as deepseek-v4.1-flash; its subscription rates are assumed equal (not published).

models.name: GLM-5.3 (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role experiment since 2026-11-05 (owner's decision): Kimi-K3.1-Pro replaced it as the top model and lane 2's worker, being cheaper and faster per passing run in the 2026-11-05 experiment; kept so the glm53 profile can still name it. low, minimal and medium are all sent as medium: equal correctness (3/3 vs 3/3, 0 empty answers, 0 malformed tool calls) and a real saving (median completion 1332->854, i.e. 35.9% fewer; median wall 26.3->17.8 s, 32.1% less), so medium is sent raw to synthetic.new; low is still never sent raw because GLM returns an empty answer (tested 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-16; measured 2026-10-17, results.md, issue #24)

models.name: Kimi-K3 (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane, only by a model-experiment profile (experiments.json). Prices, context and modalities from https://synthetic.new/pricing/models, checked 2026-11-05: the context widened from 262144 and image input was added since the 2026-10-17 check. Whether it honours reasoning_effort is unverified.

models.name: Kimi-K3.1-Pro (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role top since 2026-11-05 (owner's decision, after the Kimi-K3.1-Pro vs GLM-5.3 experiment: on two graded tasks x two copies with one model in every seat, all 8 runs passed every hidden test; Kimi-K3.1-Pro cost $0.81 in total against $2.03, median $0.20 a run against $0.38, with about 4x fewer calls, 6.6x fewer output tokens and half the wall time, though its first token was occasionally slow, p90 up to 47 s). As top it is lane 2's worker. Beta on synthetic.new's pricing page (2026-11-05). Efforts copied from Kimi-K3: a request for xhigh or max is sent as high.

models.name: GPT-OSS-120B (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane, only by a model-experiment profile (experiments.json). Added 2026-11-05 from synthetic.new's /openai/v1/models. Whether it honours reasoning_effort is unverified, so the efforts list is a conservative guess.

models.name: GLM-4.7-Flash (synthetic.new via Otari)
models.efforts_note: role experiment: never picked by a lane, only by a model-experiment profile (experiments.json). Added 2026-11-05 from synthetic.new's /openai/v1/models. Whether it honours reasoning_effort is unverified, so efforts carries a single value -- the validator refuses an empty list, and with one effort every reasoning request maps to medium.
